newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold - Indian sub-continent prices seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Gold - Indian sub-continent prices seen rising.

text.p: Gold prices in the Indian sub-continent are shaking off their lethargy and beginning to rise, aided by festival buying in India and fears of further currency depreciation in Pakistan, dealers and analysts said on Monday.
In India, gold demand has revived ahead of two major Hindu festivals falling within a month from now, and is supported by hopes of a promising harvest after a good monsoon, dealers said.
Gold prices in Bombay, India's main supply centre for precious metals, rose in the week to Monday by 20 rupees per 10 grammes to 5,130 rupees.
"There's going to be a rise in demand as buying of gold is also a religious rite during festivals," said bullion analyst Madhusudan Daga.
Hindus consider Diwali, the festival of lights, falling on November 11, as particularly auspicious for buying gold and silver.
In Karachi, gold prices gained 40 rupees per 10 grammes to 5,002 rupees in the week to Monday, which dealers said was due to fears of further depreciation of the country's currency.
They said political uncertainty had also triggered gold buying.
"We see a slight rise in gold rates this week owing to the fear of a lower adjustment of the rupee and political uncertainty," one dealer said.
Gold prices had risen last week on buying by jewellers in the Punjab province to meet seasonal demand for gold ornaments from cotton growers, the dealer said.
Bombay dealers said hopes of a good harvest in India, following an excellent monsoon, had aided the previous week's price rise.
"There will be money in villages and small towns to buy gold," said Daga. "Indians, especially in rural areas, have an undying faith in gold as an investment for the future."
Improving demand in the Indian sub-continent had arrested the recent downtrend in gold prices in Dubai, the feeder market market India and Pakistan, dealers said.
Prices of gold per 10 grammes improved marginally by one dirham to 450 dirhams in the week to Sunday.
"As Diwali gets closer demand should be stronger for the next three to four months," a trader said.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $=35.65 Indian rupees, 36.97 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay and Karachi prices October 14 & 7 and Dubai prices October 13 & 6 respectively.
